insights.ariaLabel: Information about the selected event type

facts.carrington: DONKI tracks Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) to help anticipate extreme scenarios. A solar storm similar to the 1859 Carrington Event could damage electrical grids and satellites today, so this data helps authorities protect critical systems.
facts.birthday: You can discover what the Sun was doing on the day you were born by selecting your birthday as the date range and exploring the solar events recorded on that day.
facts.mars: DONKI helps scientists study the effects of the solar wind on Mars. Because the planet does not have a strong global magnetic field like Earth, its atmosphere is more exposed to particles released by the Sun.
facts.astronauts: Space weather data helps protect astronauts by supporting radiation alerts for space missions and safety planning for future missions to the Moon.
facts.auroras: DONKI helps predict northern and southern auroras. Solar wind speed and geomagnetic activity can be used to estimate their likely intensity and location.

flr.whatIsHappening: The Sun releases enormous flashes of light and radiation. They travel at the speed of light and take only 8 minutes to reach Earth.
flr.howItAffectsYou: The radiation does not pass through the atmosphere, so we are safe, but it can disrupt radio signals used by aircraft and ships.

cme.whatIsHappening: A giant bubble containing billions of tonnes of magnetised gas is launched by the Sun into space.
cme.howItAffectsYou: When it travels towards Earth, it can push satellites out of their usual orbits and cause temporary disruptions to GPS signals on your phone.

gst.whatIsHappening: Energy from the Sun collides with and disturbs the invisible magnetic shield that protects planet Earth.
gst.howItAffectsYou: In extreme cases, it can overload electricity transformers and cause power outages. The positive side is that it can create spectacular auroras in the sky.

sep.whatIsHappening: A storm of extremely fast protons is released by the Sun, acting like a form of radioactive rain in deep space.
sep.howItAffectsYou: It is one of the greatest dangers for space travel. Astronauts on the Space Station or travelling to the Moon may need to take shelter in protected areas.

hss.whatIsHappening: The Sun has holes in its atmosphere through which a continuous stream of gases blows at millions of kilometres per hour.
hss.howItAffectsYou: It acts like the daily breeze of space. When this wind becomes stronger, it can trigger small auroras near Earth's poles.

whatIsSpaceVision.question: What is SpaceVision?
whatIsSpaceVision.keywords: platform application nasa universe space project
whatIsSpaceVision.answer: SpaceVision — NASA Data Explorer is an educational platform that brings together several official NASA data sources in one experience. It allows users to explore astronomy images, space weather, photographs of Earth, asteroids, missions and other scientific content in a visual and accessible way.

officialNasaApp.question: Is SpaceVision an official NASA application?
officialNasaApp.keywords: official nasa academic project university school
officialNasaApp.answer: No. SpaceVision is an independent academic project. The platform uses official data and services made publicly available by NASA, but it is not developed, sponsored or managed by NASA.

targetAudience.question: Who was SpaceVision created for?
targetAudience.answer: The platform was created for people interested in science, technology and space exploration, including users without advanced knowledge of astronomy. It may also be useful for students, teachers and space enthusiasts.

responsive.question: Does SpaceVision work on mobile phones and tablets?
responsive.keywords: mobile responsive tablet smartphone computer desktop
responsive.answer: Yes. The interface was developed to adapt to computers, tablets and mobile phones. Some more complex visualisations, such as 3D models, may perform differently depending on the device being used.

nasaApis.question: Which NASA APIs does SpaceVision use?
nasaApis.keywords: apod donki epic neows neowatch api astronomy weather earth asteroids
nasaApis.answer: SpaceVision uses several public NASA services:

apod.name: APOD
apod.description: Astronomy Picture of the Day — daily astronomy content accompanied by a scientific explanation.

donki.name: DONKI
donki.description: A space weather database including solar flares, geomagnetic storms and coronal mass ejections.

epic.name: EPIC
epic.description: Images of the full disk of Earth captured by the EPIC camera aboard the DSCOVR satellite.

neows.name: NeoWS
neows.description: Data about asteroids and other objects passing close to Earth's orbit.

apod.question: What is the Astronomy Picture of the Day?
apod.keywords: apod photograph video astronomy daily image
apod.answer: The Astronomy Picture of the Day, known as APOD, is content published daily by NASA. It may be a photograph, a scientific illustration or a video, accompanied by an explanation written by professionals in the field.

spaceWeather.question: What is space weather?
spaceWeather.keywords: donki sun solar flares geomagnetic storms solar events
spaceWeather.answer: Space weather studies conditions on the Sun and in space that may affect Earth and its technological systems. In SpaceVision, DONKI data allows users to explore events such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections and geomagnetic storms.

epic.question: What is the EPIC camera?
epic.keywords: epic earth dscovr satellite images planet
epic.answer: EPIC, or the Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera, is a camera installed aboard the DSCOVR satellite. From a position between Earth and the Sun, it captures images of the illuminated side of the planet at several wavelengths.

nearEarthObjects.question: What are near-Earth objects?
nearEarthObjects.keywords: asteroids neows neowatch near earth hazardous orbit distance
nearEarthObjects.answer: They are asteroids or comets whose orbits pass relatively close to Earth's orbit. This designation does not necessarily mean that there is a risk of collision. SpaceVision presents information such as distance, speed, estimated size and risk classification.

realTime.question: Is the displayed data available in real time?
realTime.keywords: real time updated nasa delay cache
realTime.answer: SpaceVision presents the latest information made publicly available through NASA APIs. Not every source operates in real time: some are updated daily, while others receive new data throughout the day.
realTime.callout: The update frequency depends on each NASA service.

updateFrequency.question: How frequently is the data updated?
updateFrequency.keywords: frequency update apod epic donki neows cache
updateFrequency.answer: APOD publishes new content every day. EPIC may provide several images per day. DONKI receives events whenever new space weather occurrences are recorded, and NeoWS is updated according to orbital data published by NASA.

noResults.question: Why do some dates have no results?
noResults.keywords: no results empty date no event error
noResults.answer: Some dates may not have images or events available. This does not necessarily mean that an error has occurred; no content may simply have been recorded for that date. Try selecting another date or increasing the search range.

mediaNotLoading.question: Why do some images or videos fail to load?
mediaNotLoading.keywords: image video failure unavailable connection youtube nasa
mediaNotLoading.answer: Some content is hosted by external services or may become temporarily unavailable. A slow connection, API limits or browser restrictions may also prevent it from loading. Refresh the page and try again a few minutes later.

accountRequired.question: Do I need to create an account to explore the website?
accountRequired.answer: No. You can access public areas without creating an account. Authentication is only required for personal features such as saving favourites, managing your profile, downloading your data or adding a personal NASA API key.

createAccount.question: How can I create an account?
createAccount.keywords: register create account name email password
createAccount.answer: Open the registration page, enter your name, email address and a valid password, and submit the form. Once registered, you can sign in and use the platform's personal features.

forgotPassword.question: I forgot my password. What should I do?
forgotPassword.answer: On the sign-in page, select the password recovery option. Enter the email address associated with your account and follow the instructions sent to you. In a development environment, the message may be recorded in the server logs.

deleteAccount.question: How can I delete my account?
deleteAccount.answer: Account deletion is available in the Profile area dedicated to account management. The action requires confirmation and removes access to the account. Before deleting it, you can download a copy of your data.

howFavoritesWork.question: How do favourites work?
howFavoritesWork.answer: After signing in, select the heart icon on compatible content. The favourite is linked to your account and can be viewed or removed on the Favourites page.

favoritesAcrossDevices.question: Are favourites available on other devices?
favoritesAcrossDevices.answer: Yes. Favourites are saved to your account and not only to the browser. When you sign in on another device using the same account, you should find the content you previously saved.

favoritesLogin.question: Why do I need to sign in to save favourites?
favoritesLogin.answer: Signing in allows each favourite to be linked to the correct user and remain available after closing the browser or changing devices. Without signing in, you can continue exploring the content, but you cannot save it to your personal collection.

whatIsNasaKey.question: What is a NASA API key?
whatIsNasaKey.keywords: api key nasa requests limit profile
whatIsNasaKey.answer: It is a personal code provided by NASA to identify requests made to its APIs. A personal key gives you your own request limit instead of relying only on the application's shared key.

personalNasaKey.question: How does the NASA API key work and why should I use a personal key?
personalNasaKey.keywords: nasa api key personal shared limit requests blocked account profile obtain create
personalNasaKey.paragraph1: SpaceVision uses a shared NASA API key so visitors can access content without configuring their own key. However, this key is shared by all platform users and has a request limit.
personalNasaKey.paragraph2: When many people use the website at the same time, that limit may be reached temporarily. In that situation, some NASA images, events or other data may stop loading until the limit becomes available again.
personalNasaKey.paragraph3: To avoid relying on the shared key, you can obtain a personal key free of charge from NASA's official API portal. After signing in to SpaceVision, you can enter it in the NASA key area of the Profile page.
personalNasaKey.callout: Get a personal key from <nasaLink>NASA's official API portal</nasaLink>.

rateLimit.question: What does “request limit reached” mean?
rateLimit.answer: It means that the key being used has temporarily reached the maximum number of requests allowed by NASA. You can wait for the limit to reset or add a personal NASA key on the Profile page.

nasaKeySecurity.question: Is my personal NASA key protected?
nasaKeySecurity.answer: The key is sent to the back end and used for requests to NASA. It should not be exposed in URLs, in the public interface or to other users. You can replace or remove it at any time from your Profile.

storedPersonalData.question: What personal data is stored?
storedPersonalData.keywords: personal data name email favourites key privacy
storedPersonalData.answer: The application stores the data required to manage the account, such as name, email address and protected password. It may also store favourites, preferences and a personal NASA key when the user chooses to add one.

passwordStorage.question: Are passwords stored as plain text?
passwordStorage.answer: No. Passwords are processed using Laravel's security mechanisms and stored as hashes. This means that the original password should not be directly readable in the database.

downloadData.question: Can I download my data?
downloadData.answer: Yes. The Profile page includes an option to download the data associated with your account. This feature allows you to review the personal information stored by the platform.

cookies.question: Does SpaceVision use cookies?
cookies.answer: The application may use technical mechanisms required for authentication and the user experience. See the Cookie Policy available in the footer for more detailed information.

connectionError.question: What should I do when a connection error appears?
connectionError.keywords: error network server backend cors connection
connectionError.answer: Check that you have an Internet connection and refresh the page. In a local environment, also confirm that both the front end and the Laravel server are running. If the problem continues, try again later or use the contact form.

supportedBrowsers.question: Which browsers are supported?
supportedBrowsers.answer: SpaceVision was developed to work in recent versions of the main browsers, including Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Some visual features may vary in older browsers or on devices without WebGL support.

keyboardSupport.question: Can SpaceVision be used only with a keyboard?
keyboardSupport.keywords: accessibility keyboard tab enter escape wcag
keyboardSupport.answer: The interface was developed with support for keyboard navigation, including menus, forms, filters, accordions and modals. Focus should remain visible when navigating with Tab, Shift + Tab, Enter and Escape.

contactTeam.question: How can I contact the team?
contactTeam.answer: You can use the contact form available on the About page. Submitted messages are made available to the platform administrators.

facts.title: Facts that sound like fiction
facts.description: The universe is stranger than you imagine.

closestPlanet.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
closestPlanet.fact: Mercury ranges from 430 °C during the day to −180 °C at night — the greatest temperature variation in the Solar System.

sunIsStar.fact: The Sun is a middle-aged yellow dwarf star, approximately 4.6 billion years old.

redPlanet.text: Which of these planets is known as the "Red Planet"?
redPlanet.fact: Mars gets its colour from iron oxide — in effect, the planet is covered in rust.

earthMoons.text: How many moons does Earth have?
earthMoons.fact: The Moon moves approximately 3.8 cm farther away from Earth every year — roughly as fast as fingernails grow.

soundInSpace.text: Explosions can be heard in space.
soundInSpace.fact: Sound needs a medium through which to travel. In the vacuum of space, there is absolute silence.

largestPlanet.text: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
largestPlanet.fact: Jupiter is so large that all the other planets in the Solar System could fit inside it together.

famousRings.text: Which of these planets has the most famous rings?
famousRings.fact: Saturn's rings are 280,000 km wide, but on average they are only 10 metres thick.

sunlightTravelTime.text: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
sunlightTravelTime.fact: When you look at the Sun, you are looking into the past: the light reaching you left approximately 8 minutes and 20 seconds earlier.

cosmicLegend.name: Cosmic Legend
cosmicLegend.description: Perfect score! The universe holds no secrets from you.

starCommander.name: Star Commander
starCommander.description: Excellent! You know the Solar System as well as your own neighbourhood.

orbitPilot.name: Orbital Pilot
orbitPilot.description: Good flight! You have already left the atmosphere — one more mission and you will reach the stars.

spaceCadet.name: Space Cadet
spaceCadet.description: Every legend begins with their first training session. Repeat the mission and surprise yourself!

earthsInsideSun.title: Earths inside the Sun
earthsInsideSun.description: More than one million Earth-sized planets could fit inside the Sun — with room to spare.

venusDay.title: Time is strange on Venus
venusDay.description: Venus takes longer to rotate on its axis than it takes to orbit the Sun.

spaceSilence.title: Space has no sound
spaceSilence.description: Without air to carry sound waves, even the largest stellar explosion is completely silent.

project.title: A digital bridge to <accent>space science</accent>.
project.paragraph1: This project was born from a deep fascination with space science and the incredible opportunity provided by the official <nasaLink>NASA Open APIs</nasaLink> programme.
project.paragraph2: We know that scientific and astronomical data can feel intimidating to the general public. That is why we created a digital bridge that organises, filters and illustrates this information in a simple, fast and intuitive way.

technology.title: Built like a real digital product
technology.description: The project combines front end, back end, authentication, databases, API integration and UX/UI principles.

items.react: Responsive interface, reusable components and an interactive experience.
items.laravel: API, authentication, security, caching and database integration.
items.nasaApis: Astronomical data, space weather and Earth observation.

hero.title: Cookie Policy

summary.label: In summary:
summary.text: SpaceVision does not use advertising cookies or third-party tracking cookies. We only store what is essential — your session and favourites — directly in your browser.

navigation.control: How to clear or disable storage

authentication.name: Authentication session
authentication.duration: Deleted when the browser tab is closed
authentication.purpose: Keep you signed in while you navigate the platform.

favorites.name: Favourites
favorites.duration: Until you clear your browser data
favorites.purpose: Store the images and captures you marked with the heart icon.

tracking.name: Advertising or tracking cookies
tracking.purpose: SpaceVision does not integrate advertising networks or third-party tracking pixels.

whatAreCookies.title: What cookies are
whatAreCookies.paragraphOneBeforeLocalStorage: Cookies are small text files that a website may ask your browser to store, usually to remember who you are between visits or to measure page usage. Your browser also provides other forms of local storage, such as
whatAreCookies.paragraphOneAfterStorage: which work in a similar way but are never sent automatically to the server with every request.
whatAreCookies.paragraphTwo: SpaceVision uses this second, lighter and more private form of storage. We refer to it as "cookies" on this page because it is the term most people recognise, but technically we do not place cookies in your browser.

howWeStore.title: How SpaceVision stores data
howWeStore.description: The following table summarises everything the application stores in your browser, what it is used for and how long it remains there.

thirdParties.title: Third-party APIs and services
thirdParties.paragraphOneBeforeLink: ) directly from your browser to retrieve images and data. These requests do not cause NASA to place cookies on your device through our application — only when you leave SpaceVision and visit
thirdParties.paragraphOneAfterLink: will you be subject to NASA's own privacy policy.
thirdParties.paragraphTwo: The service hosting this website may use technical infrastructure cookies, for example for load balancing or protection against abuse, outside the application's direct control.

control.title: How to clear or disable storage
control.description: You can delete everything SpaceVision has stored at any time without contacting our team:

items.logout: Signing out immediately deletes the stored authentication token.
items.clearBrowserData: Clearing your browser data under settings → privacy → site data removes your favourites and any active session.
items.privateMode: Private or incognito browsing does not retain anything after you close the window.

control.note: Note: clearing your browser data signs you out and empties the list of favourites stored locally.

changes.description: If the way SpaceVision stores data in your browser changes — for example, by introducing theme preferences or internal analytics — we will update this page and the date shown above before the change takes effect.

meta.title: Accessibility — SpaceVision
meta.description: Read about the accessibility measures implemented in SpaceVision and how to report difficulties using the platform.

hero.title: Accessibility statement
hero.description: SpaceVision is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive digital experience, allowing everyone to explore official NASA content and data.

commitment.title: Our commitment
commitment.description: We aim to continuously improve the platform's accessibility and follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.2, at level AA.

measures.title: Accessibility measures implemented
items: Keyboard navigation through the main features.
Semantic structure using appropriate headings, regions and HTML elements.
Accessible labels for forms and buttons.
Clear visual indication of the focused element.
Appropriate colour contrast between text and background.
Error messages presented in text form.
Use of ARIA attributes when necessary.
Responsive interface for different screen sizes.
Content that does not rely on colour alone.

compatibility.title: Compatibility
compatibility.browsers: SpaceVision was developed to work with recent versions of the main browsers, including Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge and Safari.
compatibility.assistiveTechnologies: The platform aims to support assistive technologies such as screen readers, keyboard navigation and magnification tools.

limitations.title: Known limitations
limitations.introduction: Despite the work carried out, some areas may not yet fully meet every accessibility requirement.
items: Some three-dimensional visualisations may be more difficult to use using only the keyboard.
Some content provided by NASA's external APIs may not include complete alternative descriptions.
Some scientific information may require further improvements to simplify the language.
limitations.conclusion: These limitations will be reviewed and improved progressively.

feedback.title: Contact and feedback
feedback.description: Should you encounter an accessibility barrier or have difficulty using a feature, send us a message through the contact page.
feedback.instructions: When reporting a problem, include the following whenever possible:
items: The page where you found the problem;
The browser or device you used;
The assistive technology used, where applicable.

assessment.title: Accessibility assessment
assessment.description: SpaceVision's accessibility is assessed through automated tests, manual inspection, keyboard navigation and reviews of the application's main user flows.

update.title: Statement update
update.description: This statement was updated in July 2026.

meta.title: Privacy policy — SpaceVision
meta.description: Learn how SpaceVision handles personal data, favourites, messages and account information.

layout.title: Privacy Policy
layout.description: What data SpaceVision stores, why it stores it and how you can control it.
layout.summary: We store as little as possible: without an account, we do not collect personal information. With an account, we only store what is essential for authentication and favourites — never sold or shared with third parties.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.description: This page explains what personal data SpaceVision stores, why it is stored and what you can do to access or delete that information. We collect as little as possible — only what is required for accounts and favourites to work.

data.title: What data we store

guest.stored: No personal information — you can view APOD, DONKI, EPIC and NeoWatch without providing any data.

registration.stored: Your name, email address and password. The password is always encrypted and never stored as plain text.

account.stored: The favourites you save and any profile information you edit.

contact.stored: Your name, email address and the message you send us.

data.note: We do not request payment details, precise location data or special categories of personal data, such as health information or ethnic origin.

items.favorites: Save and synchronise your favourites between sessions;
items.messages: Reply to the messages you send us;
items.security: Keep the platform secure and working correctly.

security.title: Where data is stored and how it is protected
security.database: Your account data is stored in the SpaceVision backend database and protected using reasonable technical measures. Your password is always stored in encrypted form.
security.sessionBefore: The token that keeps you signed in is stored only in your browser's
security.sessionAfter: and disappears when you close the browser tab — it is never stored indefinitely on your device.
security.callout: No system is completely immune to incidents, but we do everything reasonably possible to keep your data secure.

sharing.title: Sharing with third parties
sharing.description: We do not sell or rent your personal data. There are only two technical exceptions:
sharing.hostingAfter: where the backend and database operate;
sharing.nasaAfter: (api.nasa.gov), which are used only to retrieve data and images — we never send your personal information to these services.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.introduction: Under the GDPR, you may at any time:

items.access: Access the data we hold about you;
items.delete: Delete your account and its associated data from the Profile page;
items.complaint: Submit a complaint to the Portuguese Data Protection Authority, CNPD, if you believe your rights have not been respected.

rights.deletion: When you delete your account, your personal data and favourites are removed unless the law requires us to retain them for longer.

children.title: Children and minors
children.description: Anyone can explore SpaceVision without an account, but account creation is not intended for children under the age of 13 without the consent of a parent or legal guardian. Should we become aware that we have collected a child's data without that consent, we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.description: This policy may be updated periodically. The date shown at the top of this page always indicates the latest version.

layout.title: Terms and Conditions
layout.description: The simple rules that keep SpaceVision fair for everyone — what you can expect from the service and what we ask in return.
layout.summary: SpaceVision is a free educational project without commercial guarantees. You do not need an account to explore NASA data — only to save favourites or manage a profile.

introduction.title: Introduction and acceptance
introduction.paragraphOne: This document explains the rules for using SpaceVision, an educational platform that presents public data and images from NASA's open APIs at api.nasa.gov. It is not a commercial product — it is a project created to explore and learn from real space data.
introduction.paragraphTwo: By using the website, you agree to these rules. Should any part of them not make sense to you, we recommend that you stop using the platform and contact us.

features.title: What you can do on SpaceVision
features.introduction: You can use the website without an account to:

items.apod: View the astronomy picture of the day, APOD;
items.epic: View images of Earth captured by the DSCOVR satellite, EPIC;

features.account: You only need to create an account to save favourites or manage a profile. As this is an educational project, we cannot guarantee that the website will always be available or free from errors — its operation depends largely on NASA's own APIs.

account.title: Your account
account.introduction: Should you decide to create an account, we ask that you:

items.password: Keep your password secure and do not share it;
items.unauthorisedAccess: Tell us if you believe someone has accessed your account without permission;
items.automation: Do not use bots, intensive scraping or other automation that could overload the website or NASA APIs;
items.restrictedAreas: Do not attempt to access administrative areas or other people's accounts.

account.deletion: You can delete your account at any time from the Profile page by confirming your password.

intellectualProperty.title: Intellectual property
intellectualProperty.description: The images and scientific data displayed on SpaceVision come directly from NASA and are subject to NASA's own usage terms, generally as public-domain material. The SpaceVision design, code and brand were created specifically for this project and must not be copied or used commercially without permission.

liability.title: Availability and liability
liability.description: Because SpaceVision relies on external NASA APIs, the platform may experience outages, delays or incomplete data outside our control. We may change, suspend or discontinue features at any time without prior notice.
liability.callout: SpaceVision is provided as is, without warranties, and we are not liable for damage arising from the use of the platform or from inaccuracies in NASA data.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.description: We may update these Terms periodically. When this happens, we will update the date shown at the top of this page. Continuing to use SpaceVision after a change means that you accept the updated terms.
